predecessors.note: 'Abd al-Karim overthrows the Tunjur King Daud' in 1635; the Tunjur kingdom was 'established around the 15th century'. No dossier exists yet for the Tunjur.

land.text: the whole sultanate, 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'

successors.note: The page adds that the sultanate was 'reconstituted under French suzerainty in 1935' and joined independent Chad in 1960; those are outside the map's years for this state.

capitals.name: Wara
capitals.note: Abd al-Karim built his capital at Wara; the page gives no year or coordinates, so the point is Abéché, the later capital in the same region, as a proxy.

capitals.name: Abéché
capitals.note: Sharif made Abéché the capital; the page gives no year and places Sharif around the 1838 succession dispute, so 1838 is a bridge. The French took Abéché on 2 or 12 June 1909 (Wadai War page).

correction.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché (the gazetteer's Wadai region inside Cliopatria's outline); the page gives no extent for the first century

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1635-1803: 'In 1635, the Maba and other small groups in the region rallied to the Islamic banner of Abd al-Karim' (the page's 1635, Cliopatria's 1636). Cliopatria draws the full 280k km2 outline from the start, but the page ties the expansion to Muhammad Sabun after 1804, so the first century is the Wadai heartland (about 94k km2 of the outline).

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1636 shape unchanged, applied for 1804-1889

keyframe_review.note: 260k km2 (shapes.csv 279,943) for 1636-1889, and no page gives an area (neither the Wadai nor the Wadai War infobox has one), so no infobox comparison is possible. Holds 1804-1889: 'After 1804, during the reign of Muhammad Sabun (1804 - c. 1815)' he extended his rule south to Dar Sila and Dar Runga, with Dar al Kuti further south (undated). The outline's western edge at 15.1 E and its south are not dated by any page.
280k km2, 0.1 percent smaller than 1636: edge noise where the Mahdist State and the British lie; nothing on the pages changes in 1890.

279k km2: edge noise against French Africa from 1895; the pages give no change (the 1898-1899 Anglo-French division put Wadai in the French sphere and Darfur in the British, with 'the Wadai-Darfur borders' left disputed).
279k km2: edge noise against British Africa; no page change. Ahmad al-Ghazali, backed by Ali Dinar of Darfur, took the throne after Yusuf's death in 1898; Dud Murra overthrew him in 1901.
279k km2 for 1905-1907, edge noise. 'Open conflict between the European colonial power and Wadai broke out in 1906' (Wadai War page); the first dated battle is Dokotchi on 29 May 1908.

keyframe_review.note: 279k km2 for 1908-1910. The state lasts to 1912 ('completely occupied by the French in 1912'; infobox 1635-1912), so the shape holds 1908-1912; the French took Abéché in June 1909 and Dud Murra fought on until October 1911, so Abéché is hatched from 1909 (ledger).

region.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché (the gazetteer's Wadai region inside Cliopatria's outline); the page gives no extent for the first century

ledger.note: 1635: Abd al-Karim founds the Wadai sultanate by overthrowing the Tunjur. 'In 1635, the Maba and other small groups in the region rallied to the Islamic banner of Abd al-Karim'; infobox 'Abd al-Karim overthrows the Tunjur King Daud'. The page names no boundary, so the heartland is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the lands of Cliopatria's outline beyond the Maba heartland: Dar Sila, Dar Runga and the south and west

ledger.counterpart: Dar Sila, Dar Runga and Dar al Kuti peoples (no dossier)
ledger.note: 1804 onward: Sabun extends the sultanate south. 'After 1804, during the reign of Muhammad Sabun (1804 - c. 1815)' he extended his rule south to Dar Sila and Dar Runga; Dar al Kuti was expanded into later. The page dates none of these, so 1804 is the start of his reign (page silent).

region.text: Bagirmi, south-west of Wadai on the Chari

ledger.note: 1805: Wadai attacks Bagirmi. 'In 1805 Wadai conquered Bagirmi, killed its ruler, and captured and sold 20,000 people into slavery.' The page does not say Bagirmi was annexed, so the campaign is a contest, not a gain.
The Bagirmi campaign is a one-year event on the page: no occupation or tribute is described afterwards (page silent).

29 May 1908: the first dated French victory over Wadai forces, at Dokotchi. 'Open conflict ... broke out in 1906'; Captain Jérusalemy's column of 200 beat Wadai forces at Dokotchi on 29 May 1908 and at Djoua on 16 June 1908. The page does not locate the battles; the heartland stands for the zone.

region.text: Abéché, which the French occupied in June 1909

ledger.note: June 1909: the French take Abéché. Captain Jean-Joseph Fiegenschuh, with a column of 180, occupied Abéché on '2 or 12 June 1909'; sources differ on the day. The French installed Adam Asil as kolak in 1909 (ousted 1911).

October 1911: Dud Murra surrenders. Dud Murra was forced to surrender in October 1911 after Largeau's counter-insurgency campaign and was imprisoned at Fort-Lamy. Wadai had won at Wadi Kadja (4 January 1910) and Dorothe (8 November 1910) before.

region.text: Abéché, which the French occupied in June 1909

ledger.note: 1912: the occupation becomes annexation. Wadai was 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'; some native rulers kept de facto independence to 1917 (Cut-cut massacre).

region.text: the whole sultanate, annexed to French Africa

ledger.note: 1912: the Wadai Empire ends. Infobox '1635-1912'; 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'. Cliopatria's last year is 1910.

wars.name: Wadai-Darfur conflicts
wars.outcome: Wadai was a tributary of Darfur through the 17th century; Ya'qub Arus later refused tribute and 'Darfur attacked Wadai but was defeated'; Darfur installed Sharif in Wadai in 1838 and he quickly regained independence. The Darfur page adds that Umar Lel invaded Wadai and was captured c. 1739 and that Bukr repelled Ya'qub with Egyptian weapons. No border moved; the vassal tint is carried by the sultanate-of-darfur dossier.

wars.name: Wadai conquest of Bagirmi
wars.outcome: Wadai defeats Bagirmi, kills its ruler and enslaves 20,000 people (the page); no annexation is described.

wars.name: Wadai War

zones.text: Abéché, which the French occupied in June 1909

wars.outcome: French victory: Dokotchi (29 May 1908), Djoua (16 June 1908), Abéché (June 1909); Wadai wins at Wadi Kadja (4 January 1910) and Dorothe (8 November 1910, Maillard killed); Dud Murra surrenders in October 1911; 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'. The infobox lists Darfur, the Senussi and Dar Masalit on Wadai's side.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Wadai frontier; the 1898-1899 Anglo-French division left 'the Wadai-Darfur borders' disputed, and the Sahel edges of the outline are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened: two (budget 5), plus the Darfur page (read for sultanate-of-darfur) for the Wadai-Darfur wars. Neither Wadai page gives an area, so no infobox comparison was possible; the Wadai page is thin (no dates for Sharif, Yusuf or Ibrahim, no Fezzan or Kordofan campaigns). Cliopatria draws one 260-280k km2 outline from 1636; the dossier stages it: the Wadai heartland from 1635, the full outline from 1804 (Sabun) as a confidence-1 bridge. Not mapped for lack of a dated page: the sack of Kukawa under Sharif (the page's year was not read verbatim), Dar al Kuti, the northern trade road (opened c. 1809/10), Rabih's raids. End: 1912 (infobox, 'completely occupied by the French in 1912') against Cliopatria's 1910; the French took Abéché in June 1909 and the war ran to October 1911. The 1935 reconstitution under French suzerainty is outside the years drawn. No rulers strip: only Sabun (1804-c. 1815), Ali (1858-1874) and Yusuf (1874-1898) are dated. Counterparts needing dossiers: tunjur-kingdom, bagirmi-sultanate (af-03-x), Dar Sila, Dar Runga and Dar al Kuti. Gazetteer lacks Wara, Dokotchi, Dorothe, Dar Sila, Dar Runga, Dar al Kuti.
